title: Plural 2: Accusative and the Animacy Split
titleRussian: Множественное число 2: Винительный падеж и одушевлённость
description: In the plural, the accusative depends on animacy. Inanimate plurals reuse the nominative plural; animate plurals borrow the genitive plural. The split applies to all three genders, not just to masculines as in the singular.
descriptionRussian: Во множественном числе винительный падеж зависит от одушевлённости. Неодушевлённые существительные совпадают с именительным падежом; одушевлённые — с родительным. Это правило действует для всех трёх родов.
intro: Animacy comes back, and in the plural it is stricter than you have seen it. In the singular only masculine nouns split; here all three genders do, so feminine words for people change too. There is a wrinkle in the order: animate objects borrow the genitive plural, which you do not build until the next two lessons. For now, learn today's forms by sight and the machinery will catch up.
rules: The plural accusative depends on animacy. Inanimate plurals reuse the nominative plural form; animate plurals borrow the genitive plural form. In both cases the noun is still in the ACCUSATIVE case - it only shares a shape with the nominative or genitive.
Inanimate plural accusative = nominative plural: Маша читает книги. Антон покупает журналы. Студенты пишут письма.
Animate plural accusative looks identical to the genitive plural, but it is still the accusative (a direct object answering кого?): Маша знает братьев. Антон видит друзей. Учительница учит студентов.
The animacy split applies to ALL genders in the plural, not just to masculines as in the singular. Animate feminines switch too: вижу подруг, знаю сестёр.
Common animate object forms to learn by sight here: братьев, друзей, сестёр, подруг, учителей, студентов, детей, людей.
examples: Маша читает интересные журналы. (Masha reads interesting magazines.) журнал is inanimate, so plural acc = plural nom журналы.
Антон знает моих братьев. (Anton knows my brothers.) брат is animate, so plural acc = gen pl братьев.
Студенты пишут длинные письма. (The students are writing long letters.) письмо is inanimate, so plural acc = plural nom письма.
Учительница знает всех учителей. (The teacher knows all the teachers.) учитель is animate, so plural acc = gen pl учителей.
Маша часто видит сестёр. (Masha often sees her sisters.) сестра is animate, so plural acc = gen pl сестёр.
В магазине покупают новые телефоны. (At the shop they buy new phones.) телефон is inanimate, so plural acc = plural nom телефоны.

items.promptEnglish: There are fresh newspapers on the table.
items.hint: The noun is the subject here, and газета is feminine with a hard т. What is its plural?
items.explanation: Газета is the subject of 'there are X', so it stays in the nominative plural: газеты.

items.hint: Журнал is inanimate. What is the rule for inanimate plurals in the accusative?
items.explanation: Журнал is inanimate, so the plural accusative equals the plural nominative: журналы. Журналов is the genitive plural (used after много or нет, not as a plain object).

items.promptEnglish: Anton hasn't seen his brothers in a long time.
items.hint: Брат is animate. What form does the animate plural accusative borrow?
items.explanation: Брат is animate, so the plural accusative borrows the genitive plural: братьев. Братья is the nominative plural (a subject form).

items.hint: Подруга is an animate feminine. What form does the animate plural accusative take?
items.explanation: Подруга is animate, so the plural accusative is the genitive plural подруг, even though it is feminine. Подруги is the nominative plural (the form an English speaker reaches for). The animacy split applies to feminines too.

items.promptEnglish: The students are writing long letters.
items.explanation: Письмо is inanimate, so the plural accusative equals the plural nominative: письма.

items.promptEnglish: This school knows all its teachers.
items.hint: Учитель is animate. The animate plural accusative matches the genitive plural.
items.explanation: Учитель is animate, so the plural accusative is the genitive plural учителей.

items.hint: Сын is animate: the plural object borrows which form?
items.explanation: Animate plurals take the genitive plural as their object form: знает сыновей. Сыновья is the nominative plural (subject only).

items.promptEnglish: Anton reads interesting books in the evenings.
items.hint: Книга is inanimate: what does the plural object look like?
items.explanation: Inanimate plural objects equal the nominative plural: читает книги. Книг is the genitive plural ('нет книг'); the animacy split only redirects animate nouns.

items.promptEnglish: The teacher sees the students in the corridor.
items.explanation: Animate plural objects borrow the genitive plural: видит студентов. Студенты is the nominative plural.

items.promptEnglish: Lena meets her sisters after work.
items.hint: Сестра is an animate feminine. Watch the plural object.
items.explanation: The animacy split covers feminines in the plural: встречает сестёр (genitive plural with the fleeting -ё-). Сёстры is the nominative plural, the shape English pulls you toward.

items.promptEnglish: Masha buys flowers at the kiosk.
items.hint: Цветы is inanimate. Object form in the plural?
items.explanation: Inanimate plural objects equal the nominative plural: покупает цветы. Цветов is the genitive plural. Only animate plurals borrow the genitive.

items.promptEnglish: We see the children on the playground.
items.hint: Ребёнок is animate; its plural is irregular.
items.explanation: Дети is animate, so its object form is the genitive plural детей: видим детей. Дети is the nominative plural.

blanks: Маша часто видит _____. (Masha often sees her sisters.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Сестра is animate, so the plural accusative is the genitive plural: сестёр. Сёстры is the nominative plural.

errorCorrection.explanation: Друг is animate, so the object form is the genitive plural друзей: знает друзей. Друзья is the nominative plural, correct as a subject (друзья пришли) but not as the object of знает.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон встречает свои сёстры после работы.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton meets his sisters after work.
errorCorrection.explanation: In the plural the animacy split applies to feminines too. Сестра is animate, so the object form is the genitive plural сестёр: встречает сестёр. Сёстры is the nominative plural (the shape English pulls you toward).

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша часто читает книг по вечерам.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha often reads books in the evenings.
errorCorrection.explanation: Книга is inanimate, so its object form equals the nominative plural: читает книги. Книг is the genitive plural, correct after a quantity word or нет (много книг, нет книг) but not as a plain object. This is the opposite mistake from the animate ones: do not switch a thing to the genitive.

minimalPairs.explanation: Знать takes the accusative. Брат is animate, so the object form is the genitive plural братьев. Братья is the nominative plural ('the brothers' as a subject), which does not fit after знать.

Читать takes the accusative. Книга is inanimate, so the object form equals the nominative plural: книги. Книг is the genitive plural, used after numbers, after много, or after нет, but not as a plain object.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each direct object by whether its plural accusative keeps the nominative plural (inanimate) or switches to the genitive plural (animate).

reviewVocab.term: знать / видеть / встречать братьев, друзей, сестёр
reviewVocab.definition: to know / see / meet brothers, friends, sisters; animate plural objects take the genitive plural as their accusative form, in every gender.
reviewVocab.example: Маша знает братьев, видит сестёр и встречает подруг.

reviewVocab.definition: to read / buy books, magazines, letters; inanimate plural objects keep the nominative plural as their accusative form.
reviewVocab.example: Антон читает книги и покупает журналы.

reviewVocab.definition: children, people (plural accusative / genitive); irregular plural object forms of ребёнок and человек, both animate.
reviewVocab.example: Учителя хорошо знают детей и любят людей.
